verdict.rationale: Twenty documents a developer-first GraphQL and REST API. Every object, custom ones included, automatically gets endpoints identical to built-in objects, and a Metadata API can create, modify and delete objects, fields and relations. It also supports batch operations, outbound webhooks, an MCP server, and views-as-code through the app CLI, and a community user reports the REST API worked ok. However, nothing claims or shows full UI parity: dashboards, workflow building, permissions/role setup, and mailbox/calendar connection are described only as UI features, with no API coverage evidenced. Missing for 10: an explicit UI–API parity commitment, documented API coverage for dashboards, workflows, roles/settings and integrations, and independent hands-on confirmation of breadth.
